title: Pet Insurance Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate a monthly pet insurance premium — dog or cat, by age and cover. Enter your pet, breed size (dogs), pet's age (years), cover and area and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Estimate a monthly pet insurance premium before you get quotes: pick the pet (dog or cat), breed size, age, level of cover and area, and the calculator works out a rough monthly price from published US market averages — base premiums of about $45–$75 a month for dogs and $30 for cats, adjusted for age (older pets cost more), cover (accident-only is cheapest, wellness cover is dearest) and area. This is an estimate only, not a quote: real premiums depend on the insurer, the breed, pre-existing conditions and the excess you choose.

## How to use the Pet Insurance Calculator

Start by choosing your pet from the list, then choosing your breed size (dogs) from the list, entering your pet's age (years), choosing your cover from the list and finally choosing your area from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Pick dog or cat, breed size and age.
2. Choose the level of cover and your area.
3. Read the estimated monthly premium and the likely range.

## How it works

The [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 3-year-old medium dog with accident + illness cover in an average-cost area comes out at about $55 a month (likely range $44–$66). Try the same figures in the [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Pet: Dog, Breed size (dogs): Medium breed, Pet's age (years): 3, Cover: Accident + illness, Area: US average), the [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) returns Estimated premium: $55 per month, Likely range: $44 – $66 per month, Per year: $660. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Random Picker](/random-picker) is worth a look before you finish.

## How the estimate is built

From a base monthly premium per species and size, multiplied by three factors: age (under 1 year ×0.9, 1–3 years ×1.0, 4–6 ×1.15, 7–9 ×1.35, 10 and over ×1.6), cover (accident-only ×0.55, accident + illness ×1.0, plus wellness ×1.25) and area (average ×1.0, high-cost ×1.15, lower-cost ×0.9). The range shown is ±20% around the result. Every factor is shown on the page, so you can see exactly what the estimate assumes.

## What really decides the price

The breed (some breeds are far more expensive to insure), pre-existing conditions (usually excluded or priced in), the excess and the reimbursement percentage you choose, and the insurer. Two quotes for the same pet can differ by 50% or more, so use this estimate to sanity-check quotes, then get three real ones.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Insure a pet young — premiums rise with age and pre-existing conditions are excluded.
- Compare the excess and reimbursement rate, not just the monthly price.
- Get three real quotes — this estimate is for orientation only.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much is pet insurance?

Roughly $45–$75 a month for a dog and about $30 for a cat in the US, before age, breed and cover adjustments. Older pets and fuller cover cost more. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is pet insurance worth it?

It depends on the pet and your savings. One emergency surgery can cost several thousand dollars — insurance is for the bill you could not pay out of pocket, not for routine care. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why do premiums rise with age?

Older pets get sick more often and their treatment costs more, so insurers price that in. Insuring a pet while it is young locks in lower rates. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pet Insurance Calculator](/pet-insurance-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Pet Insurance Calculator?

Just Pet, Breed size (dogs), Pet's age (years), Cover and Area. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
